Jarczow Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Jarczów, Poland

Not demolished. Established shortly after Jarczów's founding as a private town in 1755, this cemetery gradually expanded to about 0.56 hectares by the second half of the 19th century; its oldest surviving matzevah dates to around 1760–1780. German forces destroyed it during WWII, using its tombstones to reinforce roads, though today the original 18th-century core — about 0.06 hectares — still holds more than a dozen fragmented limestone and sandstone tombstones. Two matzevot recovered from local streets have since been returned to public view: one mounted on a wall at the church square, the other placed back in the cemetery.
